name: agent-job-profiles

tasks.title: Add JobProfile dataclass and new global fields to AgentConfig
tasks.description: In agentconfig/store.py add a `JobProfile` dataclass with: `name: str = ""`, `enabled: bool = True`, search group (`keywords: list[str]`, `locations: list[str]`, `preferred_sources: list[str]`), and requirement fields ALL optional/nullable per spec §5.2 items 4-7 — `remote_model: str | None`, `employment_country: str | None`, `eor_allowed: bool | None`, `require_entity_verification: bool = True`, `salary_floor: int | None`, `salary_ask_min: int | None`, `salary_ask_max: int | None`, `working_language: str | None`, `glassdoor_min: float | None`, `glassdoor_min_reviews: int | None`, `accepted_role_types: list[str]`, `rejected_role_types: list[str]`. Give it `from_dict`/`to_dict` in the SAME defensive style the file already uses (per-key isinstance checks falling back to the default; reuse `_is_string_list`). Then extend `AgentConfig` with `profiles: list[JobProfile] = field(default_factory=list)`, `target_companies: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)`, `cooldown_days: int | None = None`, `max_applications_per_run: int | None = None`. CRITICAL CORRECTION to the spec: `AgentConfig.to_dict()` is a hand-written 4-key dict literal and `from_dict` whitelists field-by-field — this store does NOT preserve unknown keys, so every new field must be added explicitly to BOTH methods. Docstrings required; functions <=25 lines, max nesting 3.
tasks.doneWhen: `pytest tests/test_agent_config_store.py` passes, including new cases for: a full round-trip through save()/load() preserving profiles and the three new globals; defaults when the JSON is absent; an empty `profiles` list; a profile JSON entry with a wrong-typed field falling back to that field's default; and an unknown top-level key being ignored without raising.

tasks.title: Extend AgentConfigModel/AgentConfigUpdate with profiles and global fields
tasks.description: In api/schemas.py, add a `JobProfileModel(_Camel)` mirroring T1's `JobProfile`, and extend `AgentConfigModel` (line ~259) and `AgentConfigUpdate` (line ~270) with `profiles`, `target_companies`, `cooldown_days`, `max_applications_per_run` — optional on the Update model, defaulted on the response model. Add @field_validator methods in the same style as the existing `_strip_and_drop_empties` / `_validate_run_at` / `_validate_run_days`: comma-split + trim + drop-empties for EVERY multi-item field (keywords, locations, preferred_sources, accepted_role_types, rejected_role_types, target_companies) accepting either a list or a single comma-delimited string; salary values > 0 with floor <= ask_min <= ask_max when all present; glassdoor_min within 0-5; cooldown_days >= 0; max_applications_per_run >= 1; profile names non-empty and unique after trim. camelCase crosses the wire automatically via the `_Camel` base.
tasks.doneWhen: `pytest tests/test_agent_config_api.py` passes with a new reject-case test for each validator listed above.

tasks.title: Confirm and pin PUT merge semantics for profiles
tasks.description: Verify `put_agent_config` in api/routes.py (line ~709) needs no change: it does `merged = agent_config_store.load().to_dict()` then `merged.update(body.model_dump(exclude_unset=True, exclude_none=True, by_alias=False))`. Because `exclude_none=True` is set, an omitted or null `profiles` never reaches `merged`, and a supplied `profiles` replaces the stored list wholesale — which is exactly the decided semantic. Change the route ONLY if a real defect is found; otherwise leave it untouched and add the tests that pin the behaviour down. Add a short comment above the merge naming the wholesale-replacement semantic so a future reader does not 'fix' it into a deep merge.
tasks.doneWhen: `pytest tests/test_agent_config_api.py` passes with two new tests: (a) PUT with a full `profiles` list replaces the stored list wholesale rather than appending or deep-merging; (b) a PUT carrying only `runAt`/`runDays` leaves previously stored `profiles`, `targetCompanies`, `cooldownDays` and `maxApplicationsPerRun` intact.

tasks.title: Teach agent-config.js to fetch the profiles payload
tasks.description: agent/agent-config.js is a CLI, NOT a module — it has zero exports, prints to stdout and signals failure with exit codes. Its allowlist is an inline array literal on line 8: `if (!base || !["enabled", "run_at", "run_days", "llm_credentials"].includes(field)) process.exit(1);`. Add a fifth field, `job_config`, to that literal and a branch that fetches the same `/api/agent/config` URL and writes the profiles + globals (profiles, targetCompanies, cooldownDays, maxApplicationsPerRun, blockedCompanies, and any resolved company boards) to stdout as a single JSON line. Every existing branch (`enabled` scalar, `run_at` comma-join, `run_days` day-number join, `llm_credentials` three-line output) must keep its exact current output format and exit codes — those are consumed by daily-apply.sh and entrypoint.sh. Keep the 5000ms timeout and the exit-1-on-any-error contract.
tasks.doneWhen: `node agent/agent-config.js job_config` against a stub HTTP server returns valid JSON on stdout with exit 0, and returns exit 1 printing nothing when the endpoint 404s, times out, or TRUTHCV_MCP_URL is unset; `node agent/agent-config.js enabled|run_at|run_days` output is byte-identical to before the change.

tasks.title: Render profiles and globals into the run prompt
tasks.description: CRITICAL CORRECTION to the spec: agent/RUNBOOK.md is NEVER templated into the prompt — daily-apply.sh only existence-checks it at line 34 (`[[ -r "$RUNBOOK" ]] || abort ...`) and the model reads it itself because agent/prompt.md tells it to. The ONLY prompt injection point is line 82, `PROMPT="$(cat "$PROMPT_FILE")"...`, followed by the MAX_APPLICATIONS_PER_RUN cap block at lines 88-90. So: fetch `job_config` via agent-config.js, and when it yields enabled profiles, append a rendered block to $PROMPT. Per enabled profile render (a) a search-strategy block — concrete search URLs composed from keywords x locations x preferred_sources, stating the deterministic order boards -> watchlist -> WebSearch backfill — and (b) a requirements block listing ONLY the criteria that are set, each carrying waiver semantics ('if this information cannot be found, treat as waived and record it as waived'), with the entity fail-closed prose included only when require_entity_verification is true. Then render global lines: the per-run cap (config value overriding MAX_APPLICATIONS_PER_RUN env, which stays the fallback when the config field is unset), the cooldown number, and the watchlist with resolved careers URLs plus resolve-instructions for unresolved names. Finish with the any-single-enabled-profile-passes rule and an instruction to record which profile drove each application. Fetch failure OR an empty/absent profiles list must leave the prompt byte-identical to today's. ALSO in this task (folded in to avoid two plans writing this file concurrently): add `mcp__truthcv__record_company_board` to the `--allowedTools` list in this same script, so the tool registered by the MCP plan is visible to the agent.
tasks.doneWhen: A new shell-level fixture test proves three cases: (a) configured values appear verbatim in the composed prompt; (b) a profile with blank criteria emits no line for them; (c) fetch failure or empty profiles produces a prompt byte-identical to the pre-change output. `bash -n agent/daily-apply.sh` is clean and the script's allowedTools list contains `mcp__truthcv__record_company_board`.

tasks.title: Create the agent prompt-render test harness
tasks.description: CORRECTION to the spec: there is NO existing test harness of any kind for agent/daily-apply.sh, agent/entrypoint.sh or agent/agent-config.js — none exists to extend, so create one. Add agent/test-prompt-render.sh: a self-contained bash script that stubs the agent-config.js call and PROMPT_FILE, drives the prompt-composition path, and asserts the three cases named in the previous task. It must not require Docker, network, the claude CLI, or the interceptor socket. Keep it runnable standalone with `bash agent/test-prompt-render.sh` and exiting non-zero on failure. If daily-apply.sh does not already expose a seam for stubbing the config fetch, add the smallest one that works (an overridable variable holding the config-fetch command), and say so in the report.
tasks.doneWhen: `bash agent/test-prompt-render.sh` exits 0 on the current tree and exits non-zero if the profile-render block is removed from daily-apply.sh.

tasks.title: Create the company-board resolution store
tasks.description: Create companyboards/store.py (plus an empty companyboards/__init__.py) following agentconfig/store.py's pattern exactly: a `board_path()` returning `data_dir() / "company_boards.json"`, a `CompanyBoard` dataclass (`company: str`, `careers_url: str`, `ats: str = ""`, `status: str = "ok"`, `resolved_at: str = ""`), defensive per-key `from_dict`/`to_dict`, `load()` returning an empty mapping on missing/corrupt/non-dict file, and an atomic `save()` using the tmp-file + `replace()` idiom already in agentconfig/store.py.
